function.name: science_history_get_invention
function.description: Retrieve the inventor and year of invention based on the invention's name. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

The answer: Albert Einstein invented the theory of relativity, specifically the special theory of relativity in 1905, and general relativity in 1915. The question likely expects: Albert Einstein, 1905 (special relativity) or 1915 (general relativity). The user says "相對論的理論" which could refer to the theory of relativity in general. So we can mention both. We should use the function to retrieve the inventor and year. The function signature: science_history_get_invention with parameters: invention_name, want_year. We need to call the function with invention_name: "相對論" or "Theory of Relativity". The function returns inventor and year. But the function only returns year if want_year true. It doesn't return inventor. Wait: The function description: "Retrieve the inventor and year of invention based on the invention's name." It says "Return the year of invention if set to true." So it returns year if want_year true. But does it also return inventor? It says "Retrieve the inventor and year of invention". So presumably it returns both inventor and year. But the function signature only has want_year. So maybe it returns inventor always, and year optionally. So we should call with want_year true. Let's call function.
